Core Research Findings at a Glance EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Addressing the primary research questions on heavy commercial freight safety across Canada.

QUESTION 1: FREQUENCY & SEVERITY 1999–2021

Did semi collisions increase, and why did fatal share rise?

Annual road-tractor casualty collisions declined 46.5% from 4,186 in 1999 to 2,240 in 2021. However, because non-fatal injury collisions fell faster than fatal collisions, the conditional fatal share rose from 6.13% (2012–2016) to 6.96% (2017–2021). This rise reflects faster declines in minor injury recording rather than increased physical crash lethality.

QUESTION 2: HARM ASYMMETRY 2012–2021 DECADE

Who is harmed in road-tractor collisions?

Severe harm is heavily asymmetric. In the 2012–2021 historical decade, 1,581 out of 2,206 identified fatalities (71.7%) occurred in other motor vehicles (passenger cars, light trucks, vans). Tractor occupants accounted for only 15.6% of deaths (344 fatalities), while pedestrians, bicyclists, and motorcyclists accounted for 12.7%.

QUESTION 5: VKT EXPOSURE 2015–2021 TABLE 10

Do collisions track freight distance traveled?

Normalizing observed events against Transport Canada Table 10 modeled freight distance shows that casualty collisions per billion modeled VKT fell 25.5% pre-pandemic (89.9 → 67.0) and 44.5% overall (89.9 → 49.9) by 2021. Fatal events per billion VKT fell 34.7% (5.67 → 3.71), demonstrating improved safety per distance traveled.

QUESTION 7: VEHICLE AGE AUDIT V_YEAR ANALYSIS

Are older road tractors more deadly?

The data disproves the hypothesis that older trucks cause higher fatality rates. Controlling for road alignment, configuration, weather, month, and hour, tractors aged 16+ years exhibit a statistically significantly lower adjusted Odds Ratio (OR = 0.786, 95% CI: 0.65–0.96) than modern tractors (0–2 years old).

Mass-Ratio Physical Consequence: Over 71.7% of people killed in road-tractor collisions are occupants of other vehicles (cars, light trucks, SUVs). By contrast, only 15.6% of deaths are tractor drivers or passengers. This stark disparity underscores that road-tractor collisions present primary lethality risk to other road users rather than truck drivers themselves.

Freight Exposure Conclusion: Casualty collisions per billion modeled VKT declined steadily from 89.90 in 2015 to 49.92 in 2021 (−44.5%), while fatal collisions fell from 5.67 to 3.71 per billion VKT (−34.7%). Even excluding the 2020–2021 pandemic period, pre-pandemic rates fell 25.5%.

Vehicle Age (V_YEAR) Severity Audit & Adjusted Odds Ratios AUDIT & ML

Multivariable logistic regression controlling for road alignment, configuration, weather, month, and hour across 5 tractor age cohorts.

Adjusted Odds Ratio vs 0–2 Year Tractors Reference Baseline (OR = 1.00)
✅
The Aging Fleet Myth: Older commercial road tractors do not have higher conditional fatality rates. Tractors aged 16+ years show an adjusted Odds Ratio of 0.786 (95% CI: 0.646–0.957, p = 0.016), meaning they are significantly less likely to result in a fatality when a casualty crash occurs than brand new (0–2 year old) tractors.
